question.text: Investors include Foundations/Endowments in Cat III AIFs primarily because:

answer.text: They have long-term horizons and large corpuses suited to illiquidity

explanation.text: The Logic: Foundations/Endowments have long horizons and large corpuses, enabling them to bear illiquidity of Cat III AIFs. The Trap: They do NOT need daily liquidity; tax-free/mandate arguments are unfounded. Cross-Exam Context: Global hedge-fund investor profile from Section 3.3.1.1. Distributor's Pro-Tip: In India, university endowments are emerging as potential AIF investors — market to their treasury teams.
